learn.hook: Can you colour a picture, watch cartoons and eat a samosa all at once? Things can get messy!
points: The poem 'One Thing at a Time' tells us to give our full attention to one task before we start the next.
To focus means to give all your attention to one thing.
When we focus, our work is neater and we finish it faster.
Things that pull our attention away, like a TV that is on, are called distractions.
The poem also says there is a time for work and a time for play.

example.q: Read this poem: When I draw, I only draw, / I do not watch TV. / When I read, I only read, / The words come clear to me. / When work is done, I run to play, / And laugh the whole bright day! Question: What does the child do after the work is done?
steps: Find the line that begins 'When work is done'.
So the child plays only after finishing the work.
example.answer: The child runs out to play.

learn.reallife: Switch off the TV while you do homework. You will finish quicker and have more time to play!

games.title: Match the word to its meaning
pairs: something that takes your attention away
a piece of work to do

games.title: Focus: true or false?
items: Doing one thing at a time helps us do it well.
Full attention makes our work neater and better.
A loud TV helps you focus on sums.
A loud TV is a distraction.
The poem says there is a time for work and a time for play.
The child plays after the work is done.
Focusing means doing five things at once.
Focusing means giving attention to one thing.
Keeping your desk tidy can help you focus.
A tidy desk has fewer things to distract you.

quiz.q: Poem lines: "When I draw, I only draw, / I do not watch TV." What does the child do while drawing?
quiz.explain: The child says 'I only draw' and does not watch TV.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice the word 'only'

quiz.q: Poem lines: "When I read, I only read, / The words come clear to me." Why are the words clear?
options: The child reads with full attention
quiz.explain: Reading with full focus helps the child understand the words.
quiz.mistake: Does not link focus with understanding

quiz.q: Poem line: "When work is done, I run to play." When does the child play?
quiz.explain: The child plays only after the work is finished.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the time clue 'When work is done'

quiz.q: Which pair of words rhymes in the poem?
quiz.explain: 'Play' and 'day' end with the same '-ay' sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks words that appear near each other but do not rhyme

quiz.q: What does 'focus' mean?
options: To give full attention to one thing
quiz.explain: When you focus, all your attention is on one thing.
quiz.mistake: Thinks focus means doing more things at once

quiz.q: Which child is focusing on the work?
options: Ravi reads while playing a video game
Asha does her sums with the TV off
Meena writes while chatting with a friend
quiz.explain: Asha has no distraction, so she can give full attention to her sums.
quiz.mistake: Thinks doing two things at once is focusing

quiz.q: What is the main message of the poem?
options: Do one thing at a time with full attention
quiz.explain: The poem says to focus on one task and to play after work.
quiz.mistake: Picks one small detail instead of the main idea

quiz.q: Poem line: "And laugh the whole bright day!" How does the child feel?
quiz.explain: Laughing shows the child is happy.
quiz.mistake: Does not use 'laugh' as a clue to feelings

teach.ask: Gappu is eating, singing and doing homework all at once. The homework is a mess! What should Gappu do?
teach.praise: Yes! Do one thing at a time with full focus, and play after the work is done. Gappu's homework will be neat now!
teach.nudge: How many things should Gappu do at one time? And when should Gappu play?

topics.title: Work and play: one and many

learn.hook: One toy, two toys. One box, two... boxs? No! Let us find out the right way.
points: Work like homework and helping at home comes first. Play time is more fun when work is done.
To make most nouns plural (more than one), add -s: toy → toys, book → books.
Add -es to words ending in s, x, ch or sh: bus → buses, box → boxes, watch → watches, brush → brushes.
If a word ends in a consonant + y, change y to i and add -es: story → stories. But day → days, because 'a' comes before y.
Some words change in a special way: child → children, tooth → teeth, foot → feet, mouse → mice, leaf → leaves.

example.q: Think it through: what is the plural of 'hobby'?
steps: The letter before y is 'b', a consonant.
So change y to i and add -es.

learn.reallife: Count things in your room: two pencils, three boxes, four brushes. Saying them aloud is plural practice!

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'box'?
quiz.explain: Words ending in x take -es: boxes.
quiz.mistake: Adds only -s to a word ending in x

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'story'?
quiz.explain: Story ends in a consonant + y, so y changes to i and we add -es.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s without changing y

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'child'?
quiz.explain: 'Child' has a special plural: children.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s to every noun

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'leaf'?
quiz.explain: In 'leaf', f changes to v and we add -es: leaves.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s without changing f to v

quiz.q: Fill in: "Ravi packed three ___ into his school bag."
quiz.explain: Three means more than one, so we add -s: books.
quiz.mistake: Adds -es where only -s is needed

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'brush'?
quiz.explain: Words ending in sh take -es: brushes.
quiz.mistake: Adds only -s to a word ending in sh

quiz.q: Which of these is a chore (work) you can do at home?
quiz.explain: Folding clothes is a job that helps at home. The others are games.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up work and play

quiz.q: "Finish your homework first, then go out to play." Why is this a good plan?
options: You never have to do homework
You can play freely with no work left
Homework is more fun than games
quiz.explain: When the work is finished, you can enjoy playing without worry.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the plan means no play at all

teach.ask: Gappu has one kite and you give him two more. Gappu says 'three kites', but for 'box' he says 'three boxs'. Help Gappu!
teach.praise: Great! For more than one we usually add -s, but words ending in x, s, ch or sh take -es. Three boxes, Gappu!
teach.nudge: What do we add to 'box' to make it more than one?

topics.title: Action words: verbs in the present

learn.hook: Run, read, draw, jump! A sentence cannot work without an action word.
points: A verb is an action word. It tells what someone or something does: run, read, eat, sing.
We use the simple present tense for things we do every day: I play cricket every evening.
With I, you, we and they, the verb stays the same: I play, they play.
With he, she, it or one person's name, add -s: Asha plays. Add -es after s, x, ch, sh or o: watches, goes.
If a verb ends in a consonant + y, change y to i and add -es: fly → flies, cry → cries.

example.q: Think it through: choose the right verb. 'Meena (read / reads) a story every night.'
steps: Meena is one person, so she is like 'she'.
With she, we add -s to the verb.
example.answer: Meena reads a story every night.

learn.reallife: Tell someone your daily routine: I wake up, I brush my teeth, I go to school. Those are present-tense verbs!

items.text: My mother ___ the plants every day.

quiz.q: Which word is a verb?
quiz.explain: 'Write' is an action word.
quiz.mistake: Picks a naming or describing word

quiz.q: Fill in: "My brother ___ to school by bus."
quiz.explain: With one person (he), 'go' becomes 'goes'.
quiz.mistake: Adds only -s to 'go'

quiz.q: Fill in: "The baby ___ when she is hungry."
quiz.explain: Cry ends in a consonant + y, so it becomes cries.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s without changing y to i

quiz.q: Fill in: "We ___ our homework after lunch."
quiz.explain: With 'we', the verb stays the same: do.
quiz.mistake: Adds -es even when the subject is 'we'

quiz.q: Fill in: "Asha ___ her hands before eating."
quiz.explain: Wash ends in sh, so with 'she' it becomes washes.
quiz.mistake: Adds only -s to a word ending in sh

quiz.q: Find the verb in "Kabir paints a big kite."
quiz.explain: 'Paints' tells what Kabir does.
quiz.mistake: Picks the noun or the describing word

quiz.q: Fill in: "The cat ___ milk."
quiz.explain: The cat is 'it', so we add -s: drinks.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add -s with 'it'

quiz.q: Fill in: "Rohan and Meera ___ chess on Sundays."
quiz.explain: Rohan and Meera are two people (they), so the verb stays 'play'.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s even when there are two people

teach.ask: Gappu says 'Gappu fly every day.' Something is wrong. What is a verb, and how should Gappu say it?
teach.praise: Super! A verb is an action word. For one bird we say 'Gappu flies'. Gappu is flapping happily!
teach.nudge: What kind of word is 'fly'? And how does it change for just one bird?
